title: Thiaroye massacre
summary: On 1 December 1944, French officers shot West African soldiers (tirailleurs sénégalais) at the Thiaroye camp near Dakar. The men, freed from German captivity and awaiting demobilisation, had demanded back pay they were owed. French archives, read literally, record 35 deaths; earlier research suggests 300 to 400. A 2025 Senegalese white paper reported that a senior officer planned the repression.

uncertainty.note: Exact day given by both sources.

where.historical_name: Thiaroye military camp, near Dakar, French West Africa (colonial Senegal)

importance.justification: A colonial army killed returning African soldiers over unpaid wages; the toll and the cover-up are still being investigated.

audience_note: Describes soldiers shot by army officers and a disputed death toll; no graphic detail.
